abstract.p: The use of large language models (LLMs) for evaluating outputs is becoming an increasingly effective and scalable approach. However, it remains uncertain whether this capability ex tends beyond taskspecific evaluations to more general assessments of text quality, particularly in multilingual contexts. In this study, we intro duce, MTQEval, a novel framework for multi lingual text quality evaluation that learns from examples of both high and lowquality texts, adjusting its internal representations. To de velop MTQEval, we first automatically gener ate text quality preference data and then use it to train opensource base LLMs to align with ratings of high and lowquality text. Our com prehensive evaluation across 115 languages demonstrates the improved performance of the proposed model. Upon further analysis, we find that this enhanced evaluation capability also leads to notable improvements in downstream tasks.
